title: 1980s Olympic Distance: Coe vs Ovett
description: A British rivalry, a Moscow swap, and a Korean 10K—five steps into 1980s Olympic distance running.
imageHint: The classic oval track with distinctive lane markings where athletic legends were made

questions.question: At the boycotted 1980 Moscow Games, which Brit won the men's 800m—the race Seb Coe later called the worst of his life?
questions.explanation: Coe was the world-record favorite and took silver. Six days later he got revenge in the 1500m, with Ovett settling for bronze.

questions.question: Six days after Ovett beat him at 800m, Coe redeemed himself by winning which event in Moscow?
questions.explanation: Jürgen Straub of East Germany took silver; Ovett bronze. Coe remains the only man to win Olympic 1500m gold twice.

questions.question: After his Moscow 1500m gold, Coe defended that title at which 1984 Games, outsprinting favorite Steve Cram?
questions.explanation: He pulled away on the final turn and won by about six meters. He also took 800m silver again—this time behind Brazil's Joaquim Cruz.

questions.question: At those same Los Angeles Games, which Romanian won the women's 3000m after Mary Decker and Zola Budd tangled?
questions.explanation: Decker clipped Budd and fell. Puică stayed clear for gold. Budd, running barefoot for Britain, finished seventh; Decker did not finish.

questions.question: Four years after Los Angeles, which Moroccan set an Olympic record to win the men's 10,000m in Seoul?
questions.explanation: His 27:21.44 held off Italy's Salvatore Antibo. Aouita, Morocco's other star that Games, took 800m bronze instead.

easterEgg.title: They swapped events
easterEgg.text: In Moscow, each Brit won the other's specialty: Ovett took Coe's 800m, Coe took Ovett's 1500m. British fans got two golds and a lifelong argument about who was better.
